title: Countable vs Uncountable
objectives: Use countable vs uncountable accurately in A2 contexts.
Understand form, meaning, and typical usage.
Produce short spoken and written examples.
canDo: I can classify nouns and choose correct quantifiers.

warmUp.title: Activate prior knowledge
warmUp.prompt: Before this lesson, recall what you know about countable vs uncountable. How is it similar or different from Portuguese?
reflectionQuestions: When do native speakers use countable vs uncountable?
Can you think of one example?

explanation:
Countable: one apple, two apples | Uncountable: rice, information (no plural *informations)

Some/any/a lot of work with both; much/many depend on type

grammar.title: Countable vs Uncountable
grammar.rule: Countable: one apple, two apples | Uncountable: rice, information (no plural *informations)

reading.title: Countable vs Uncountable in Context
reading.text: Can I give you some advice? The furniture is new. There isn't much information on the website. These chairs are comfortable — we need many chairs for the event.

questions.question: What is the main topic of the text?
questions.explanation: The text illustrates this lesson topic.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5–7 sentences) using countable vs uncountable. Use at least 3 words from the vocabulary list.
rubricHints: Use the target structure at least twice.
writing.modelAnswer: Useful information. Good advice. Modern furniture. Good news!

tutorHints: Correct gently and ask the learner to reformulate.
Use English for meta-language when possible at A2.
